ImageDescription.value:
An advertisement for Pears' Soap, from the 1890s, instructing whites to promote cleanliness among other races.
The central part of the image shows an elderly white man in a naval uniform washing his hands in a boat cabin. In the upper corners of the ad there are two boats in the ocean and in the lower left corner of the ad we see the unloading of Pears’ Soap cargo from a ship. The lower right corner of the ad shows a white man handing over soap to a kneeling black man completely naked except for the strap covering his genitals. The caption below the picture says: “The first step towards lightening The White Man’s Burden is through teaching the virtues of cleanliness”. It is followed by text: “Pears’ Soap is a potent factor in brightening the dark corners of the earth as civilization advances, while amongst the cultured of all nations it holds the highest place – it is the ideal toilet soap”.

ObjectName.value: Boy washing hands

Categories.value: Stimming|Autistic people|Boys hand washing

ImageDescription.value: This is a photo of me, Soap, around three years old. I was standing on the cabinet door handle because I wasn't supposed to be washing my hands. I either didn't see the stepstool or was too small to move it on my own. What looks like water overflowing may be because I was at the sink for quite some time and did not want to turn it off. I am certain that I was stimming, but so far as I know, this is not a common stim. My mother is the one who took the photo, but I've labeled this as own work because it is part of the family photo collection and is, after all, a photo of me.

Categories.value: Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR|Images from Oxfam East Africa|Images from Oxfam East Africa need checking|Sanitation in Rwanda|Kigeme refugee camp|Boys hand washing

ImageDescription.value:
These handwashing facilities are based on a common Rwandan model - there is one tank for water and another for liquid soap. These are both operated by pressing down on a foot pedal. Typically Oxfam just installs a single washstand holding water with soap kept by the sink. However, in a busy camp soap can often go missing, so this innovation of having a separate tap with liquid soap means that soap supplies are always available.

Photo: Laura Eldon/Oxfam
